Implementation Plan

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8291` @ `26e1608fd0d43e7963455590a2a75ca182376682` (integration branch mismatch: false).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends `needs_human_park`
Scope-mode justification: The needs-human digest, the parking itself, and the 3-round cap from P6a are already on this branch (`scripts/operator_step_issue.py` `needs_human_park`, `scripts/unblock_judge.sh` op `needs_human`, `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` `needs_human_park_project`). This issue changes only how the one CRITICAL page per parking is decided. Today it is derived from `newly_parked`, a guess made on one digest read that nothing persists. Two concurrent judge runs for the same item can both see "not yet listed" and both page, because `unblock_judge_dispatch.yml` has no concurrency group. Nothing records whether an attempt was made, whether it succeeded, or the message ID. This plan replaces that guess with a claim marker written to GitHub before any Telegram call, plus a confirm step. Both callers share that one mechanism instead of each gaining its own. Re-entry, the epoch reset, and the digest `remove` subcommand from the wider P6 plan are not in this issue's title, so they are not planned here. Boil-the-Lake check: also attempting the alert on any successful park call that lists the item (not only when `newly_parked` is true) costs a few lines. It closes the case where the first attempt was skipped for missing configuration, so it is included. That follows §6: correctness comes before speed.

## Functions or modules to implement

**Introduction / wiring (§20.E)**
- No new script, workflow, supervisor, or database work. Everything extends existing modules.
- Entry points are unchanged:
  - the unblock judge (`.github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml` via `unblock_judge_dispatch.yml`, dispatched by `run_unblock_scan`);
  - the poller tick (`.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml`), which runs `needs_human_park_project`.
- Both workflows already pass `TG_BOT_SECRET`, `TG_ADMIN_CHAT_ID` / `TG_CHAT_ID` and `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL`, so no YAML change is needed. No entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

**1. `scripts/operator_step_issue.py`**
- `_needs_human_park_digest` / `needs_human_park`: add a `parking` key to every return dict.
  - When the item has a digest entry, it is that entry's `parked=` stamp. On an existing entry this is the preserved stamp; on a new or created digest it is the new `stamp`.
  - When the item is in the overflow list, or was counted as dropped, it is the literal `overflow`.
  - On the disabled/skip path it is `None`.
  - Existing keys (`issue`, `url`, `item`, `outcome`, `newly_parked`, `entries`, `overflow`) stay unchanged (§10).
- New constants:
  - `NEEDS_HUMAN_ALERT_MARKER_RE`, matching a last line of `^<!-- ai:unblock-park-alert:v1 item=(\d+) parked=(<ISO-Z>|overflow) state=(attempted|confirmed)(?: message=(\d{1,20}))? -->$`;
  - `NEEDS_HUMAN_PARKING_RE`, which validates the `--parking` argument.
  - The `ai:unblock` prefix is deliberate (see D1).
- New `needs_human_alert_claim(repo, item, parking, trusted_login=None, now=None) -> dict`:
  1. Validate repo, item and parking (on failure raise `UsageError`). If `needs_human_enabled()` is false, return `{"claimed": False, "reason": "disabled"}` with no API call.
  2. Resolve the login with `_resolve_login`. Read the item's comments once with the existing `load_entry_comments` (one paginated read).
  3. Count only claims written by the trusted login whose last non-empty line matches the marker regex with `item == N`. A claim matches this parking when its `parked` equals `parking`, or when it is `overflow` (see D2). If one exists, return `{"claimed": False, "reason": "already_attempted", "state": ..., "comment_id": ...}`.
  4. Otherwise POST one comment to `repos/{repo}/issues/{item}/comments`. Body: one plain sentence ("Needs-human alert attempt recorded for this parking; the needs-human digest lists this item."), then a blank line, then the marker `item=N parked=<parking> state=attempted`. Read the new comment `id` from the response. Any `_gh` failure, or a missing or non-integer id, raises `ApiError`, and the caller does not send.
  5. Re-read the comments once (paginated). The claim wins only if its id is the lowest-id matching trusted claim. If another claim has a lower id, return `{"claimed": False, "reason": "lost_race"}`. If our own claim is not visible yet, return `{"claimed": False, "reason": "claim_unverified"}`. If the re-read fails, raise `ApiError`.
  6. On a win, return `{"claimed": True, "comment_id": id, "alert_attempted_at": now_iso}`.
- New `needs_human_alert_confirm(repo, item, parking, comment_id, message_id) -> dict`:
  - Validate both IDs as positive decimal integers of at most 20 digits; otherwise raise `UsageError`.
  - Make one PATCH to `repos/{repo}/issues/comments/{comment_id}` with the same body text and marker `state=confirmed message=<id>`.
  - Return `{"confirmed": True}`. A `_gh` failure raises `ApiError`.
- `_needs_human_log` reuse: every claim/confirm outcome logs one line on stderr: `NEEDS_HUMAN_ALERT item= parking= outcome=claimed|skip|confirmed|failed reason=`.
- `main`: add `needs-human alert-claim` (`--repo --item --parking [--trusted-login]`) and `needs-human alert-confirm` (`--repo --item --parking --comment-id --message-id`). The current `elif args.command == "needs-human":` falls through to prune for any subcommand. Change it to dispatch on `digest_command` explicitly, so `prune` keeps working.
- Module docstring:
  - Replace "The caller sends the single CRITICAL alert when `newly_parked` is true" with the claim → send → confirm contract.
  - Add the new subcommands, the marker, and the API budget.

**2. `scripts/tg_helpers.sh`**
- New `tg_alert_configured LEVEL`. It returns 0 only when `TG_BOT_SECRET` is non-empty, `_tg_chat_id` is non-empty, and `_tg_should_send LEVEL` passes. This makes `ALERT_MSG_LEVEL=SILENT` count as not configured. It does no I/O and changes no existing function.

**3. `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`**
- New `unblock_needs_human_alert ITEM PARKING TEXT`, which sources `tg_helpers.sh` the same way `unblock_tg` does:
  1. If `tg_alert_configured CRITICAL` is missing or fails, log `NEEDS_HUMAN_ALERT ... outcome=skip reason=telegram_unconfigured` and return 0. No claim is made.
  2. Run `unblock_py "${SUPPORT_DIR}/scripts/operator_step_issue.py" needs-human alert-claim --trusted-login "${UNBLOCK_LOGIN}"`. If it exits non-zero, or `.claimed != true`, log and return 0 without sending.
  3. Capture the message ID with `msg_id="$(tg_send_msg "${TEXT}" CRITICAL 2>/dev/null || true)"`.
  4. If `msg_id` matches `^[0-9]+$`, run `alert-confirm`. A confirm failure only logs `outcome=failed reason=confirm_write_failed`, with no resend. Otherwise log `outcome=unconfirmed reason=send_failed_or_ambiguous`, with no retry.
- In the `needs_human)` case:
  - Replace the `if jq -e '.newly_parked == true'` block. On a successful park, read `.parking`. When it is non-empty, call `unblock_needs_human_alert` with the current message text (unchanged wording).
  - `ops_failed` handling stays as it is. Alert outcomes never set `ops_failed`.

**4. `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` — `needs_human_park_project`**
- Replace the `newly_parked` → `tg_notify` block with the same claim → send → confirm sequence. Use `python3 scripts/operator_step_issue.py` and `--trusted-login "${UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN}"`.
- Configuration check: `_smoke_fixture_alert_silenced CRITICAL` counts as not configured, and so does `tg_alert_configured CRITICAL` returning non-zero. Guard with `declare -F` in both cases; no claim is made.
- Build the same message text `tg_notify` builds today: base text plus the `Tracking:` and `Run:` URLs via `_gh_url`. Send with `tg_send_msg ... CRITICAL`. When a message ID comes back, call `tg_store_msg_id "${TRACKING_NUM}" "${msg_id}"` (guarded with `declare -F`) to keep the current `tg_send_tracked` tracking, then confirm.
- The function still never fails the tick (`return 0`).
- Update the comment block above it: "one CRITICAL alert per newly parked project" becomes "at most one persisted CRITICAL alert attempt per parking".

## Data structures affected
- New trusted comment marker in the unblock ledger family, posted on the parked item (for a project, on its tracking issue):
  `<!-- ai:unblock-park-alert:v1 item=<n> parked=<YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ|overflow> state=attempted|confirmed[ message=<telegram message id>] -->`
  - The comment's `created_at` is the persisted `alert_attempted_at`.
  - `state=confirmed` plus `message=` together hold `alert_confirmed` and the returned message ID.
- `needs-human park` JSON output gains the `parking` key. The digest body format and the entry marker regex (`<!-- ai:needs-human:entry ... parked=... -->`) are unchanged.

## API or interface changes
- New CLI subcommands: `operator_step_issue.py needs-human alert-claim` and `needs-human alert-confirm`. Each prints one JSON line on stdout and exits 0 ok, 1 bad arguments, 2 GitHub failure (the existing convention).
- New shell function `tg_alert_configured`. New judge function `unblock_needs_human_alert`.
- New log prefix `NEEDS_HUMAN_ALERT`, registered through the agents.d fragment.
- No env vars, labels, or workflow inputs are added or renamed. `NEEDS_HUMAN_DIGEST_ENABLED=false` still disables park, and so the alert path too.
- GitHub API budget per park call that reaches the alert path (§14): 2 paginated comment reads on the item, 1 comment POST, at most
